Properties can now join Expedia Group’s global travel marketplace through their existing connectivity software, with a few clicks, and go live in less than 24 hours, the company said in a Tuesday (Oct. 20) press release.
This simpler path is enabled by Expedia Group’s new Autonomous Onboarding, according to the release.
With Autonomous Onboarding, properties can go to their existing connectivity software, select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, review and accept their agreement, and connect, the release said.

Expedia Group launches AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING, helping properties access global travel demand faster
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Properties can join Expedia Group through their existing software and go live in under 24 hours.
The launch gives properties a simpler path to Expedia Group's consumer brands, B2B network and AI agentic bookings.
Five connectivity partners across multiple markets shaped the experience in pilot: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
SEATTLE, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today announced AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING™, a faster, simpler way for properties to join its global travel marketplace without leaving the connectivity software they already use. With just a few clicks, properties can select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, accept their agreement and go live in less than 24 hours - without a separate onboarding workflow or duplicate data entry.
Properties select Expedia Group as a distribution channel within their existing connectivity provider, review and accept their agreement, and connect – with no separate onboarding process and no re-entering information across systems.
From there, work that once required manual setup now happens automatically. Expedia Group's technology reaches into the property's existing software and transfers the critical data needed to set up the hotel, including room types, rates and rate plans, photos, amenities, payment setups, availability, and other property details. That data is then validated by Expedia Group, so the property can go live quickly.
Once live, properties can reach travelers through Expedia Group's multiple consumer brands, its B2B distribution network of more than 75,000 partners and 200,000 travel advisors, and its emerging AI-powered travel partnerships. Expedia Group's platform saw more than one billion average monthly searches and recorded more than 415 million booked room nights in 2025, giving properties access to significant global demand1.
Ahead of the launch, Expedia Group partnered with five pilot providers to bring Autonomous Onboarding to life: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
"Adding a new source of demand should not add a new layer of work," said Chris Hodges, VP of Global Connectivity & Partner Solutions, Expedia Group. "Autonomous Onboarding makes it much easier for properties to join Expedia Group through the technology they already use. It is an important first step in our broader vision for AUTONOMOUS DISTRIBUTION, where partners can spend less time on manual processes and more time growing their business."
Autonomous Onboarding is the first phase of Expedia Group's Autonomous Distribution journey. Beginning with onboarding, the longer-term vision is to make the full distribution lifecycle simpler and more intelligent, extending into how partners manage and, over time, optimize their business.

Expedia Group, Inc. (EXPE) Trades Below Its Old Earnings Multiple. Is AI a Real Threat to Growth?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:12 PM CDT 5 min read
Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) is entering a new phase of the online travel debate. Artificial intelligence may become another channel through which people book rooms, or it may weaken the ability of established booking platforms to attract travelers directly. Expedia Group, Inc.'s September 23 announcement that it would work with Meta's Muse assistant puts both possibilities into focus. The company could supply bookings to a new interface, but it may also surrender part of the customer relationship to whoever controls that interface.
Expedia Group, Inc. ranks eighth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit. Its ranking is based on hedge fund positioning, not a claim that its travel business is immune to disruption. Which of the seven stocks above it attracted stronger institutional interest, and how many face an equally direct challenge to their customer relationships?
Muse is not Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s only attempt to monetize traffic it does not originate. A September 22 advertising collaboration with Redion extended the company's advertising business into travel insurance, building on a longstanding protection-services relationship. Neither announcement includes a disclosed near-term contribution to earnings, however. Their importance lies in whether Expedia Group, Inc. can earn commission or advertising revenue when trip discovery moves away from its own websites.
The operating data leave room for both interpretations. In second-quarter 2026 coverage, Expedia Group, Inc.'s gross bookings rose 12%, with business-to-business bookings expanding 21% and B2B revenue rising 23%. That partner business had delivered twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit booking growth. A booking made through a bank, airline or other partner does not depend on an Expedia consumer visiting its own app, supporting an argument that the platform can adapt to new distribution models.
However, Morgan Stanley's September 16 downgrade identified a different problem: monthly active users were flat year-over-year, compared with growth of roughly 6% at Booking.com and 10% at Airbnb, according to the bank's estimates. If customer acquisition becomes more expensive while direct traffic stagnates, incremental booking revenue may require more marketing spending. Our earlier report on Morgan Stanley's Expedia Group, Inc. downgrade examines why rising B2B bookings did not fully answer the bank's concern about consumer engagement.
The Seeking Alpha data places Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) at 17.07 times trailing GAAP earnings and 14.76 times forward GAAP earnings. On a non-GAAP basis, the forward P/E is 13.07 times, compared with the company's five-year average of 23.84 times and the sector median of 14.84 times. Forward enterprise value to EBITDA is 7.94 times, versus 9.30 times for the sector and 8.91 times for Expedia Group, Inc.'s five-year average. The shares therefore carry a discount on several forward measures, though the relevant issue is whether the earnings behind those measures can hold up.
The same consensus projects EPS growth of 32.54% for 2026, slowing to 16.72% in 2027, 14.33% in 2028, and 3.45% in 2029. At the current share price, implied estimated earnings multiples descend from 13.07 times in 2026 to 11.20 times in 2027, and 9.79 times in 2028. That trajectory assumes Expedia Group, Inc. continues converting bookings into rising per-share profit while AI-related disruption remains manageable. It does not price a proven collapse in the intermediary model, nor does it guarantee that one will not occur.
There is a balance-sheet dimension to the discount as well. The data shows $7.13 billion of cash and $5.69 billion of debt, leaving net cash of approximately $1.44 billion before other obligations. It also places trailing price-to-cash-flow at 6.32 times against an 8.79-times sector median. Cash generation and repurchases can support per-share earnings during slower organic growth, but neither can permanently protect the multiple if the cost of winning travel bookings rises.
Wall Street Is Debating the Speed, Not Just the Direction
Wells Fargo cut its target to $275 from $307 on October 7 while maintaining Equal Weight, expecting the third quarter to mark a low point in room-night growth and describing choppy demand. Truist reduced its target to $288 from $309, keeping Hold, and warned that the AI threat was still more clearly visible in sentiment than in demonstrable profit erosion. Morgan Stanley took the firmer Underweight stance at $235, citing weaker consumer differentiation and risks from suppliers selling directly.
Those views differ in severity but meet at the same question: how much future distribution and marketing expense should be embedded in today's earnings estimates?
A useful comparison is Airbnb, whose inventory and direct traffic may be harder for AI booking agents to reproduce. Why does Airbnb's growth command a different valuation, and how does that comparison change the Expedia Group, Inc. debate? Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s strength in partner distribution is real; the difficulty is deciding how much protection it provides if consumer-facing discovery migrates elsewhere.
Institutional Positioning Shows the Disagreement
Hedge fund holders declined from 62 in Q1 to 55 in Q2 2026. Meanwhile, reported short interest increased from 5.20 million shares on August 31 to 7.92 million on September 30, representing 8.50% of the float. Those observations cannot identify why individual investors traded, but they provide context for a valuation that appears undemanding relative to its history. A separate Booking-versus-Airbnb comparison illustrates how margins, proprietary supply and cash flow can reshape the online travel valuation hierarchy.
For Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE), the deciding variables are partner bookings growth, consumer user retention and whether any AI-driven bookings preserve sufficient economics to support consensus EPS.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of EXPE as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. There are plenty of reasons the travel industry is struggling these days. Inflation has made some people rethink their plans. Trade wars and immigration policies have discouraged many international tourists from visiting the U.S., but one other big factor is the price of hotel rooms.
Since 2020, the average daily hotel rate has jumped from $103 to $162, a 58% rise over five years. And a new class-action suit, filed in the Western District of Washington, says the travel site Expedia is to blame.

The suit alleges the company "has abused its monopoly power to impose exclusionary contracts and pricing algorithms on hotels in violation of the federal antitrust laws." That, it says, has resulted in consumers having to pay "artificially inflated prices" for hotel rooms across the U.S.
In addition, the complaint alleges, consumers pay higher rates regardless of whether they use Expedia's online site or the hotel's official website.
Expedia, in a statement to Moneywise, denied all these allegations.
"The allegations in the lawsuit are meritless," a spokesperson said. "For over 30 years, Expedia has brought transparency to shopping for travel, allowing travelers to see different travel options, make informed travel decisions, and get competitive offerings and better value from travel suppliers."
Expedia's commissions are at the heart of the problem, says the suit. The site charges hotels a 15% commission on bookings made through one of its online portals. That, argue the plaintiffs, has resulted in hotels charging travelers as much as 30% more to recoup any lost profits.
Expedia is the flagship site of Expedia Group, a conglomerate that controls several of the biggest online travel portals, including Hotels.com, Vrbo, Travelocity, Hotwire, Orbitz, and Trivago. The lawsuit alleges 80% of all U.S-based online bookings happen on one of the company's sites.
"Expedia's anticompetitive Scheme has injured virtually every consumer who has booked a U.S. hotel room — whether through Expedia or not," the suit reads.
The plaintiffs are proposing two different classes to the court: People who booked a hotel room directly with the facility and another for people who booked online. The suit is seeking both financial penalties and a permanent injunction that would prevent the travel site from re-imposing its allegedly exclusionary contracts and pricing algorithms.

Hotels are just a part of the travel equation for tourists. And they're not the only field seeing big price increases.
Airfares have increased 22.4% over the past year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. And, for people who prefer to drive to their destination, the average price of gas has jumped roughly 40% in the past year, says AAA.
Despite the higher prices, 71% of the people surveyed by PwC in May said they planned to spend the same or more on summer travel as they did the year prior. The average spend per consumer worked out to $2,892.

New Expedia Group report identifies the travel trends set to shape 2027, from one-night getaways and carefree escapes to emerging destinations and the new Set-Jetting forecast.
LONDON, October 14, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today unveiled Unpack '27: The Trends in Travel™, the annual report exploring the destinations, experiences, and behaviours expected to shape travel in 2027.
Drawing on first-party insight from Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo, as well as global traveller research and social listening, Unpack '27 reveals the new places drawing travellers in 2027 and some surprising things they're doing when they get there.
"Travel is about creating memories, and Unpack '27 uncovers the destinations and experiences shaping those moments," said Ariane Gorin, CEO of Expedia Group. "In 2027, travellers are being more intentional in choosing their next adventure, seeking experiences that are more personal and purposeful to them. We're making it easier to discover, plan, and book the right trip, so travellers can spend less time managing the details and more time enjoying the moments that matter."
2027 Destinations of the Year — Expedia's Destinations of the Year showcases some of 2027's fastest-growing travel destinations, using real search data to track where traveller interest is climbing:
South Lake Tahoe, California, U.S. (+195%)
The Tweed, New South Wales, Australia ✓ (+35%)

Un-Adulting — Travellers are reclaiming childlike joy with getaways built around play, spontaneity, and zero obligations. With Expedia data showing 57% of travellers are likely to book an Un-Adulting trip in 2027,7 theme park events just for grown-ups, immersive attractions, and nostalgic experiences are becoming the ingredients for a genuine break from being an adult. British travellers say Un-Adulting trips are about having fun and enjoying a carefree day out (74%), quality time with loved ones (64%), and a break from everyday responsibilities (60%).*
Among the Un-Adulting experiences to try in 2027 are Tokyo Disneyland, Tokyo, Japan; Color Factory Chicago, Chicago, U.S.; Park Xcaret, Cancun, Mexico; and Gold Coast: Dreamworld. See the full list of Un-Adulting experiences.
Trip Snacking — In addition to saving for one big annual holiday, travellers are fitting more frequent, bite-sized breaks into busy lives, with searches on Hotels.com for one-night stays up nearly 10% year over year.3 Quick getaways, Brits say, are for seeing a show (49%), celebrating a milestone (42%), and resetting between longer trips (23%).7
Evidence shows that Trip Snacking is fast becoming the default way younger travellers get away. While 79% of travellers say they're planning to book a one-night stay in the coming year, that figure climbs to 83% among Gen Z and Millennials.7
Globally, a few of the most searched destinations for Trip Snacking in 2027 are Las Vegas, U.S.; Montreal, Canada; London, U.K.; Tokyo, Japan; and Paris, France.3 Learn more about Trip Snacking and see the full list of top destinations.
Gothic Getaways — The hotel stay is becoming an experience in its own right, with Hotels.com finding 56% of travellers having booked a hotel specifically for its atmosphere or aesthetic.7 Gothic Getaways are especially popular among Gen Z and Millennials, with 71% reporting a desire to stay in Gothic-style property.7 Among British travellers interested in booking a Gothic-style hotel, the leading motivations are historic hotels or castles (51%) and destinations steeped in folklore, legend, or the supernatural (41%). Additionally, many find the dramatic architecture and visual atmosphere of Gothic-style hotels appealing (40%).*
Gothic architecture, candlelit corridors, dark colour palettes, and properties steeped in history are redefining the idea of atmosphere, while demand for castle properties on Hotels.com increased 20% globally year over year4 — proving that where travellers stay can be as memorable as where they go.
Top properties for Gothic Getaways include L'oscar London, London, U.K.; Maison Métier, New Orleans, U.S.; L'Escape, Seoul, South Korea; and the Grand Hôtel Stockholm, Stockholm, Sweden. Find out more about Gothic Getaways and the hotels that embody the trend.
Set-Jetting — Five years after Expedia Group first named Set-Jetting as a travel trend, screen-inspired travel continues to turn fictional worlds and filming locations into real-world itineraries. Nearly 1 in 5 travellers now report having booked a trip to a destination after seeing it featured in a TV show or film.7
Nearly half of the travellers surveyed reported proactively researching or booking trips to destinations from upcoming TV shows and movies that haven't even been released yet, rising to 58% among Gen Z and Millennials.7 Searches for Monaco on Expedia Group properties spiked by over 120% in the 30 days after Emily in Paris Season 6 was confirmed to be filming there. And on social media, mentions of traveling to Miami increased by 64% year-over-year driven by the upcoming Miami Vice reboot.6
The 2027 forecast includes Emily in Paris Season 6, The White Lotus Season 4, Heated Rivalry Season 2, The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, Miami Vice '85, K-Pop: The Debut, Beach Read, Day Drinker, and the Ocean's Eleven prequel. These anticipated releases are putting destinations on travellers' maps before the first episode or scene arrives. Learn more about Set-Jetting.
Vrbo: Hobby Hubs — For a growing number of travellers, trip planning starts with a passion rather than a destination, with Vrbo research showing 68% are likely to take a hobby-focused trip in 2027.8 Learn more about Hobby Hubs.
Heartland Hideouts — Beach and mountain getaways may be the first destinations that come to mind when considering holiday home rentals, but Vrbo has seen dramatic growth in interest for landlocked destinations. Find all the top Heartland Hideouts.

Airbnb (ABNB) vs. EXPE and TCOM: Can Double-Digit Growth Offset Rising Regulatory Pressure?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:45 AM CDT 7 min read
Is ABNB a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Airbnb, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ABNB. Airbnb, Inc.'s share was trading at $163.23 as of October 8th 2026. ABNB's trailing and forward P/E were 34.15 and 25.38 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a vacation rental platform pitched as a great investment. ABNB shares gained 33.69% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Expedia Group (EXPE) gained 19.39% during the same period. Why are travel stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?
Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB)'s Chesky says App can become an ‘Amazon for services’
In July, we published an article about the 8 Best Stocks to Buy Following Federal Reserve Pivot Expectations and ABNB ranked #4 in that article. ABNB returned 11.54% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ABNB. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ABNB. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) operates a global online marketplace connecting hosts and guests for stays, experiences, and services. The big question for investors is whether Airbnb can keep growing beyond home rentals into hotels, Experiences, Services, advertising, and AI-powered travel tools, even as regulators tighten the rules around short-term rentals. Airbnb's business model requires little capital, runs on healthy margins, and its bookings are growing faster than major rivals in online travel.

In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, revenue rose 17% year over year to about $3.6 billion, and the number of nights and experiences booked grew 10%, outpacing 6% growth at Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE) and 5% at Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG). Over the past twelve months, revenue grew 13.6% to roughly $13.2 billion. Even so, the stock trades at about 39.8 times trailing earnings, well above the peer median of roughly 26.7 times, meaning investors are already paying up for several more years of strong growth to materialize. You can check out whether Booking or Airbnb is the better stock to buy here.
The bullish case is built on Airbnb continuing to outgrow the broader travel market by using its large base of travelers and hosts to expand into new categories. The company is adding boutique and independent hotels, Experiences, Services, sponsored advertising, smarter fees, and AI-powered search, and it says artificial intelligence has already cut the time it takes to build and launch new features by as much as 60%. Airbnb is also on solid financial footing, holding about $9.6 billion in net cash after accounting for its debt, and it generated $4.6 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2025.
Management expects revenue to keep growing at least in the low double digits for all of 2026, signaling confidence that this isn't just a one-quarter boost. If artificial intelligence keeps improving how well the platform converts browsers into bookings, and if hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising start contributing more meaningfully, bulls see multiple future growth drivers rather than reliance on home rentals alone. Consensus estimates call for earnings per share of $5.30 looking ahead, about 24% higher than the $4.26 posted over the past year, which would help justify the stock's premium valuation if it plays out. That said, Airbnb has only beaten Wall Street's earnings estimates once in its last four reported quarters, missing the other three by an average of 6%, so it still has to prove it can turn growth into consistently stronger profits.
Wall Street is only moderately optimistic about the stock from here. The average analyst price target sits at $180.57, about 6% above the current share price of $169.63, while the analysts are split fairly widely: the most bullish target of $220 implies roughly 30% upside, while the most bearish target of $125 implies about 26% downside. Given that the stock already trades near 40 times trailing earnings, investors should watch closely whether Airbnb's growth, margins, and expansion into new products stay strong enough to support that price tag. The wide spread in analyst targets shows how much disagreement there is about what happens if growth slows or execution stumbles.
Regulation is a key risk to watch. Airbnb needs enough legally available listings in major tourist cities to keep growing its bookings, but rules are moving in the opposite direction. Barcelona plans to eliminate short-term rental licenses entirely by 2028, and London, Paris, and Rome have already added various caps and restrictions. A new European Union data-sharing framework could also make it easier for local governments to find and remove listings that don't comply with the rules. On top of that, a weaker job market, slower economic growth, or rising travel costs could push cautious travelers toward cheaper options and dent bookings. With regulatory pressure building and the stock still priced near 40 times trailing earnings, there isn't much room for growth to slow down without the valuation starting to look expensive.
Hedge fund positioning shows a cautious signal. As per our database, 75 hedge funds held Airbnb, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 87 the quarter before. That drop suggests institutional investors grew more cautious on the stock even as its underlying growth and margins remained strong, hinting at unease about how long that growth can support its rich valuation. By comparison, Booking Holdings was held by 92 hedge funds, down from 95, Expedia Group was held by 55 hedge funds, down from 62, and Trip.com Group (NASDAQ:TCOM) was held by 28 hedge funds, down from 38. Booking Holdings held onto the most stable institutional support, Trip.com Group saw the sharpest pullback, and Airbnb, Inc.'s decline in hedge fund interest was steeper than Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG)'s despite Airbnb's stronger growth numbers.
Short interest data also paints a fairly cautious picture. About 3.50% of Airbnb, Inc.'s available shares are sold short, higher than Booking Holdings at 2.62% and Trip.com Group at 1.90%, though still lower than Expedia Group at 6.75%. This suggests investors are more skeptical of Airbnb, Inc.'s premium price tag and regulatory exposure than they are of Booking Holdings or Trip.com Group, but less skeptical than they are of Expedia Group.
ABNB's forward P/E is 25.38. Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group, Inc., and Trip.com Group Limited trade at forward P/Es of 13.28, 11.29, and 11.72, respectively. ABNB's own forward P/E was 27.47 at the end of 2025, so its multiple has fallen approximately 8%, but investors still pay roughly twice as much for each dollar of expected earnings as they would for its peers. We believe 25.38 times forward earnings is a demanding valuation for a stock like ABNB. This means investors who buy ABNB at this valuation are pretty much betting that faster booking growth and expansion into new categories will keep earnings growing strongly for several years. Airbnb, Inc.'s earnings per share were $4.26 over the past year, while the supplied consensus estimate is $5.30 looking ahead. This puts its expected earnings growth rate at approximately 24%. We believe ABNB's expected earnings growth could justify its premium if the company delivers on those forecasts. Its expansion into new categories offers room for further gains, but at 25.38 times forward earnings, investors are paying for continued success rather than buying an obvious bargain.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) by Chit Chat Stocks in May 2025, which highlighted Experiences and Services as drivers of engagement, user spending, and expansion beyond accommodations. ABNB's stock price has appreciated by approximately 19.32% since our coverage. We believe ABNB could be a good long-term investment, provided its earnings growth lives up to expectations.

Properties can join Expedia Group through their existing software and go live in under 24 hours.

SEATTLE, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today announced AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING™, a faster, simpler way for properties to join its global travel marketplace without leaving the connectivity software they already use. With just a few clicks, properties can select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, accept their agreement and go live in less than 24 hours - without a separate onboarding workflow or duplicate data entry.
Properties select Expedia Group as a distribution channel within their existing connectivity provider, review and accept their agreement, and connect – with no separate onboarding process and no re-entering information across systems.
From there, work that once required manual setup now happens automatically. Expedia Group's technology reaches into the property's existing software and transfers the critical data needed to set up the hotel, including room types, rates and rate plans, photos, amenities, payment setups, availability, and other property details. That data is then validated by Expedia Group, so the property can go live quickly.
Once live, properties can reach travelers through Expedia Group's multiple consumer brands, its B2B distribution network of more than 75,000 partners and 200,000 travel advisors, and its emerging AI-powered travel partnerships. Expedia Group's platform saw more than one billion average monthly searches and recorded more than 415 million booked room nights in 2025, giving properties access to significant global demand1.
Ahead of the launch, Expedia Group partnered with five pilot providers to bring Autonomous Onboarding to life: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
"Adding a new source of demand should not add a new layer of work," said Chris Hodges, VP of Global Connectivity & Partner Solutions, Expedia Group. "Autonomous Onboarding makes it much easier for properties to join Expedia Group through the technology they already use. It is an important first step in our broader vision for AUTONOMOUS DISTRIBUTION, where partners can spend less time on manual processes and more time growing their business."
Autonomous Onboarding is the first phase of Expedia Group's Autonomous Distribution journey. Beginning with onboarding, the longer-term vision is to make the full distribution lifecycle simpler and more intelligent, extending into how partners manage and, over time, optimize their business.

Expedia Group, Inc. (EXPE) Trades Below Its Old Earnings Multiple. Is AI a Real Threat to Growth?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:12 PM CDT 5 min read
Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) is entering a new phase of the online travel debate. Artificial intelligence may become another channel through which people book rooms, or it may weaken the ability of established booking platforms to attract travelers directly. Expedia Group, Inc.'s September 23 announcement that it would work with Meta's Muse assistant puts both possibilities into focus. The company could supply bookings to a new interface, but it may also surrender part of the customer relationship to whoever controls that interface.
Expedia Group, Inc. ranks eighth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit. Its ranking is based on hedge fund positioning, not a claim that its travel business is immune to disruption. Which of the seven stocks above it attracted stronger institutional interest, and how many face an equally direct challenge to their customer relationships?
Muse is not Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s only attempt to monetize traffic it does not originate. A September 22 advertising collaboration with Redion extended the company's advertising business into travel insurance, building on a longstanding protection-services relationship. Neither announcement includes a disclosed near-term contribution to earnings, however. Their importance lies in whether Expedia Group, Inc. can earn commission or advertising revenue when trip discovery moves away from its own websites.
The operating data leave room for both interpretations. In second-quarter 2026 coverage, Expedia Group, Inc.'s gross bookings rose 12%, with business-to-business bookings expanding 21% and B2B revenue rising 23%. That partner business had delivered twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit booking growth. A booking made through a bank, airline or other partner does not depend on an Expedia consumer visiting its own app, supporting an argument that the platform can adapt to new distribution models.
However, Morgan Stanley's September 16 downgrade identified a different problem: monthly active users were flat year-over-year, compared with growth of roughly 6% at Booking.com and 10% at Airbnb, according to the bank's estimates. If customer acquisition becomes more expensive while direct traffic stagnates, incremental booking revenue may require more marketing spending. Our earlier report on Morgan Stanley's Expedia Group, Inc. downgrade examines why rising B2B bookings did not fully answer the bank's concern about consumer engagement.
The Seeking Alpha data places Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) at 17.07 times trailing GAAP earnings and 14.76 times forward GAAP earnings. Forward enterprise value to EBITDA is 7.94 times, versus 9.30 times for the sector and 8.91 times for Expedia Group, Inc.'s five-year average. The shares therefore carry a discount on several forward measures, though the relevant issue is whether the earnings behind those measures can hold up.
The same consensus projects EPS growth of 32.54% for 2026, slowing to 16.72% in 2027, 14.33% in 2028, and 3.45% in 2029. That trajectory assumes Expedia Group, Inc. continues converting bookings into rising per-share profit while AI-related disruption remains manageable. Cash generation and repurchases can support per-share earnings during slower organic growth, but neither can permanently protect the multiple if the cost of winning travel bookings rises.

Those views differ in severity but meet at the same question: how much future distribution and marketing expense should be embedded in today's earnings estimates?
A useful comparison is Airbnb, whose inventory and direct traffic may be harder for AI booking agents to reproduce. Why does Airbnb's growth command a different valuation, and how does that comparison change the Expedia Group, Inc. debate? Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s strength in partner distribution is real; the difficulty is deciding how much protection it provides if consumer-facing discovery migrates elsewhere.

A separate Booking-versus-Airbnb comparison illustrates how margins, proprietary supply and cash flow can reshape the online travel valuation hierarchy.
For Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE), the deciding variables are partner bookings growth, consumer user retention and whether any AI-driven bookings preserve sufficient economics to support consensus EPS.

Expedia's commissions are at the heart of the problem, says the suit. The site charges hotels a 15% commission on bookings made through one of its online portals. That, argue the plaintiffs, has resulted in hotels charging travelers as much as 30% more to recoup any lost profits.

"Expedia's anticompetitive Scheme has injured virtually every consumer who has booked a U.S. hotel room — whether through Expedia or not," the suit reads.
The plaintiffs are proposing two different classes to the court: People who booked a hotel room directly with the facility and another for people who booked online. The suit is seeking both financial penalties and a permanent injunction that would prevent the travel site from re-imposing its allegedly exclusionary contracts and pricing algorithms.

Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) operates a global online marketplace connecting hosts and guests for stays, experiences, and services. The big question for investors is whether Airbnb can keep growing beyond home rentals into hotels, Experiences, Services, advertising, and AI-powered travel tools, even as regulators tighten the rules around short-term rentals. Airbnb is also on solid financial footing, holding about $9.6 billion in net cash after accounting for its debt, and it generated $4.6 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2025.
Management expects revenue to keep growing at least in the low double digits for all of 2026, signaling confidence that this isn't just a one-quarter boost. If artificial intelligence keeps improving how well the platform converts browsers into bookings, and if hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising start contributing more meaningfully, bulls see multiple future growth drivers rather than reliance on home rentals alone. Consensus estimates call for earnings per share of $5.30 looking ahead, about 24% higher than the $4.26 posted over the past year, which would help justify the stock's premium valuation if it plays out. Given that the stock already trades near 40 times trailing earnings, investors should watch closely whether Airbnb's growth, margins, and expansion into new products stay strong enough to support that price tag. The wide spread in analyst targets shows how much disagreement there is about what happens if growth slows or execution stumbles.
Regulation is a key risk to watch. Airbnb needs enough legally available listings in major tourist cities to keep growing its bookings, but rules are moving in the opposite direction. Barcelona plans to eliminate short-term rental licenses entirely by 2028, and London, Paris, and Rome have already added various caps and restrictions. A new European Union data-sharing framework could also make it easier for local governments to find and remove listings that don't comply with the rules. On top of that, a weaker job market, slower economic growth, or rising travel costs could push cautious travelers toward cheaper options and dent bookings. With regulatory pressure building and the stock still priced near 40 times trailing earnings, there isn't much room for growth to slow down without the valuation starting to look expensive.

ABNB's forward P/E is 25.38. Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group, Inc., and Trip.com Group Limited trade at forward P/Es of 13.28, 11.29, and 11.72, respectively. We believe 25.38 times forward earnings is a demanding valuation for a stock like ABNB. This means investors who buy ABNB at this valuation are pretty much betting that faster booking growth and expansion into new categories will keep earnings growing strongly for several years. We believe ABNB's expected earnings growth could justify its premium if the company delivers on those forecasts. Its expansion into new categories offers room for further gains, but at 25.38 times forward earnings, investors are paying for continued success rather than buying an obvious bargain.

facts.text: Expedia Group's new Autonomous Onboarding allows hotels to join its global marketplace via existing connectivity software in under 24 hours.
Expedia Group raised revenue guidance to USD 16.05 billion-USD 16.22 billion for fiscal year 2026.
Expedia Group will report third quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026.
BTIG Research reiterated a Buy rating for Expedia Group stock with a USD 400.00 price target.
Expedia Group's new Autonomous Onboarding allows hotels to join its global marketplace via existing connectivity software in under 24 hours.
Expedia Group launched AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING, allowing properties to join through existing software and go live in under 24 hours.
Five connectivity partners: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain, and Eviivo shaped the pilot experience.
Autonomous Onboarding is the first phase of Expedia Group's Autonomous Distribution journey to simplify distribution lifecycle.
Expedia Group has more than 75,000 B2B partners and 200,000 travel advisors in its distribution network.
Expedia's 15% commission on bookings has allegedly caused a 58% rise in average daily hotel rates from $103 to $162 since 2020, according to a class-action lawsuit.
Expedia Group's Unpack '27 report identifies five travel trends for 2027: Destinations of the Year, Un-Adulting, Set-Jetting, Hobby Hubs, and Heartland Holidays.
50% of Australian travellers are likely to book an Un-Adulting trip in 2027, which involves carefree getaways with play, spontaneity, and zero obligations.
Nearly 1 in 5 travellers have booked trips to destinations featured in TV shows or movies, with 57% of Gen Z and Millennials researching or booking trips to upcoming shows and movies.
88% of travellers are likely to take a hobby-focused trip in 2027, with holiday rentals used for activities like photography retreats and board-game nights.
Searches for inland Australian destinations like Canberra (+55%) and Mount Hotham (+40%) have risen significantly in 2026.
Expedia Group's Unpack '27 report identifies seven travel trends for 2027, including one-night getaways, hobby-led trips, and emerging destinations.
Niagara-on-the-Lake, ON is listed as a 2027 Destination of the Year by Expedia.
48% of Canadian travellers are likely to book an 'Un-Adulting' trip in 2027, which focuses on play, spontaneity, and zero obligations.
Searches for one-night stays on Hotels.com increased nearly 10% year-over-year, with 85% of Millennials planning to book such stays in 2027.
78% of travellers are likely to take a hobby-focused trip in 2027, with vacation rentals becoming gathering places for hobbies like photography and board games.
Expedia's Unpack '27 report identifies Set-Jetting as a trend with 57% of Gen Z and Millennials booking trips to destinations from upcoming TV shows and movies.
Expedia's Destinations of the Year report shows The Tweed, New South Wales, Australia has a 35% increase in search interest from September 2025 to July 2026.
57% of Kiwi travellers are likely to book an Un-Adulting trip in 2027, with motivations including carefree days (76%) and breaks from responsibilities (61%).
The Lord of the Rings remains the top set-jetting driver with 27% of travellers booking trips to New Zealand for its filming locations.
Expedia Group's Unpack '27 report identifies South Lake Tahoe as a 2027 destination with 195% search growth.
57% of travelers are likely to book an Un-Adulting trip in 2027, featuring theme parks and nostalgic experiences.
Hotels.com searches for one-night stays increased 10% year over year in 2027.
56% of travelers booked hotels specifically for their atmosphere or aesthetic in 2027.
Searches for Monaco on Expedia Group properties spiked by 120% after Emily in Paris Season 6 filming there was confirmed.
Analyst price target for Airbnb is $180.57, 6% above current share price of $169.63.
Expedia has become the Official Travel Partner of the NHL in North America, gaining marketing rights and designations in the U.S. and Canada.
Expedia will have brand presence on NHL's digitally enhanced dasherboards during regular season and Stanley Cup Playoffs.
Expedia serves as the presenting sponsor of the Stanley Cup Playoffs Bracket Challenge and Second Chance Bracket.
The partnership includes Expedia's exclusive rights in Online Travel, Vacation Rentals, and Hotels.
Expedia will be involved in NHL events like All-Star Weekend, Heritage Classic, Winter Classic, and Stadium Series.
Expedia's One Key loyalty program offers OneKeyCash rewards for eligible bookings.
Expedia marks its 30th anniversary in 2026 as a leading online travel agency.
Airbnb's trailing P/E is 34.15, forward P/E is 25.38 according to Yahoo Finance.
Expedia Group (EXPE) gained 19.39% over the last 12 months.
Expedia Group will report third quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026.
Expedia Group will report third quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026 via webcast and earnings release.
Jefferies adjusted Expedia's price target to $350 from $375.
Goldman Sachs adjusted Expedia Group's price target to $310 from $370.
Wells Fargo adjusted Expedia Group's price target to $275 from $307.

AI improvements could boost Airbnb's conversion rates and new product adoption
risks: AI disruption could weaken Expedia's ability to attract travelers directly
Declining monthly active users (flat YoY vs. 6% growth at Booking.com and 10% at Airbnb)
Rising B2B bookings not fully offsetting consumer engagement risks
Increased marketing costs if customer acquisition becomes more expensive
Regulatory pressure from cities like Barcelona, London, Paris, and Rome
Economic slowdown or rising travel costs reducing bookings
